title: Qualify the storage guard and first-build hooks on native Windows x86_64
goal: CEO direction 2026-11-11 ("run it all on windows too"). T-CLAUDESTORAGEGUARD-1..4 were built and tested on Linux x86_64 only; the authoring session had no Windows host (no SSH connection, no Windows toolchain), and a Linux build is not evidence that Windows works. An agent on a native Windows x86_64 MSVC host runs the acceptance below on current main, records the counts under `results`, fixes what fails in its own scoped change, and closes this record. Also run, in a fresh clone whose core.hooksPath is unset: `cargo build --offline --locked -p susi` and confirm `git config --local --get core.hooksPath` prints `.githooks`; then `cargo run --offline --locked -p xtask --bin local-snapshot -- guard` twice against origin and confirm 0 findings, with the second run reporting every ref unchanged. Points to watch on Windows: paths with backslashes or 8.3 short names as file remotes in the fixtures, `git ls-remote`/`for-each-ref` line endings, and the console-window rule for the `git` child processes.

criteria: On x86_64-pc-windows-msvc: `cargo test --offline --locked -p susi-harness --lib -- storage_guard a_harness_submission` passes (6 tests on Linux).
`cargo test --offline --locked -p xtask --bin local-snapshot --test git_publisher_native_hook --test native_push_policy` passes (31 + 7 + 17 on Linux).
`cargo test --offline --locked -p susi --test no_console_window --test architecture_tests --test lean_core_ceilings` passes.
A fresh clone's first build sets core.hooksPath=.githooks, and `local-snapshot guard` reports 0 findings against origin.

host: needs a native Windows x86_64 MSVC host
